title: Adaptive Computation Time for Recurrent Neural Networks
takeaway: A canonical early formulation of learning how much computation each input needs.
why: Establishes adaptive compute as a first-class modeling variable rather than a fixed architectural constant.

title: Universal Transformers
takeaway: Reuses a Transformer block across depth and optionally learns per-position computation time.
why: A direct ancestor of modern looped and recurrent-depth Transformers.

title: Block-Recurrent Transformers
takeaway: Adds a recurrent memory state that is updated block by block while preserving parallel computation within each block.
why: Shows how recurrence can be used as memory, not only as extra depth.

title: Looped Transformers as Programmable Computers
compute: fixed block repeated in a loop
takeaway: Demonstrates that shallow Transformers placed in a loop can emulate iterative programs and general-purpose computation.
why: Makes the connection between looped Transformers and iterative algorithms explicit.

title: Scalable Adaptive Computation for Iterative Generation
takeaway: Recurrent Interface Networks recycle latent states across iterative generative steps through self-conditioning.
why: A useful bridge from iterative generative modeling to recurrent reasoning architectures.

title: Training Large Language Models to Reason in a Continuous Latent Space
compute: hidden state fed back as next input
takeaway: Coconut replaces some explicit thought tokens with recurrent continuous hidden states.
why: One of the clearest modern examples of moving reasoning from language space into latent state space.

title: Scaling up Test-Time Compute with Latent Reasoning: A Recurrent Depth Approach
takeaway: Scales test-time compute by iterating a recurrent block rather than emitting more reasoning tokens.
why: Directly operationalizes the question: what if thinking longer means deeper latent computation?

title: PonderLM-2: Pretraining LLM with Latent Thoughts in Continuous Space
compute: extra latent steps before token emission
takeaway: Adds latent computation steps before emitting each token and studies scaling the number of those steps.
why: Provides a clean per-token alternative to visible chain-of-thought for allocating extra compute.

title: LoopFormer: Elastic-Depth Looped Transformers for Latent Reasoning via Shortcut Modulation
takeaway: Trains looped models to remain useful across different compute budgets rather than at one fixed recurrence depth.
why: Targets elastic depth and train-test consistency, central issues for practical recurrent reasoning.

title: PonderLM-3: Adaptive Token-Wise Pondering with Differentiable Masking
takeaway: Learns where extra computation should be allocated instead of applying the same number of latent steps to every token.
why: Pushes the field from 'more compute' toward 'selective compute'.

title: Loop, Think, & Generalize: Implicit Reasoning in Recurrent-Depth Transformers
takeaway: Studies systematic generalization and depth extrapolation, including the failure mode of overthinking.
why: Connects recurrence to compositional generalization and asks when additional loops stop helping.

title: Parcae: Scaling Laws For Stable Looped Language Models
takeaway: Treats looping as a dynamical system, stabilizes recurrence, and studies scaling laws for train- and test-time loops.
why: Makes stability and scaling of recurrent depth explicit scientific objects.

title: Universal Transformers Need Memory: Depth-State Trade-offs in Adaptive Recursive Reasoning
takeaway: Studies a trade-off between scratchpad memory capacity and pondering depth in recursive reasoning.
why: Highlights that reasoning compute may be jointly determined by state capacity and recurrent depth.

title: Solve the Loop: Attractor Models for Language and Reasoning
takeaway: Reframes iterative refinement around convergence to fixed points and trains with implicit differentiation.
why: A direct bridge between reasoning architectures and dynamical-systems / equilibrium-model language.

title: Latent Recurrent Transformer: Architecture Exploration, Training Strategies, and Scaling Behavior
takeaway: Adds a lightweight recurrent latent pathway across token positions while preserving standard attention and KV-cache interfaces.
why: Shows a practical route to recurrent computation without explicit pause tokens or repeated full passes.

title: Flow Reasoning Models: Turning Discrete Flows into Efficient Recurrent Reasoners
takeaway: Turns discrete flow models into recurrent reasoners that repeatedly refine predictions through self-conditioning.
why: One of the clearest points where generative flows and iterative reasoning architectures directly meet.

title: Maglev: Sliding Recurrent Memory
takeaway: Uses a stronger prefiller to supervise recurrent memories used by a sliding-window decoder.
why: Represents a complementary axis: recurrent state as memory rather than extra recurrent depth.

title: Thinking with Looped Flows
state: recurrent hidden state coupled to flow state
compute: probability-flow integration on a finer time grid
takeaway: Trains recurrent computation with local denoising objectives and spends more test-time compute by refining the temporal grid.
why: A strong recent example of combining flow objectives, recurrence, and scalable test-time reasoning.

title: Path Independent Equilibrium Models Can Better Exploit Test-Time Computation
takeaway: Path independence across initializations is strongly associated with exploiting extra inference iterations on harder examples.
why: A direct precursor to the attractor/fixed-point view of scalable latent reasoning.

title: Fixed-Point Reasoners: Stable and Adaptive Deep Looped Transformers
takeaway: Uses fixed-point convergence as an end-to-end halting mechanism and adapts recurrent compute to task difficulty.
why: Connects stability, convergence, and compute allocation in one recurrent architecture.

title: Self-conditioned Flow Map Language Models via Fixed-point Flows
compute: Flow time × fixed-point iteration; then distillation
takeaway: Interprets self-conditioning as fixed-point iteration and separates flow progress from recurrent refinement into two computational axes.
why: Provides a mathematical bridge between flow dynamics and recurrence.

title: One-step Language Modeling via Continuous Denoising
state: Continuous denoising state over token encodings
takeaway: Shows continuous denoising over language can support competitive few-step and one-step generation.
why: Supplies the generative-flow substrate later reused by fixed-point and reasoning-oriented flow models.

title: ELF: Embedded Language Flows
compute: Continuous-time flow matching with final discretization
takeaway: Keeps language generation in continuous embedding space until the final discretization step.
why: Relevant to which continuous state space is suitable for language-level flow dynamics.
